entries.title: Jeremiah 50:2
segments:
Set up a standard; the tidings of Babylon's fall are to be spread by signals as well as words. 
 
  Bel--Merodach; idols of Babylon. 
 
  Her idols are confounded; they are put to shame, because they could not save those who trusted in them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:3
segments: A nation; the Medes and Persians, whose country lay to the north-east of Babylon.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:4
segments: The children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together; the ten tribes who had been carried captive by the Assyrians, at least a remnant of them, united themselves with the Jews on their return to Palestine under Cyrus.  Thus was fulfilled the prophecy of Ezekiel,

; though a still higher fulfilment of it may be reserved for the future. 
 
It is when God's people seek his face with weeping and supplication that he interposes for their deliverance, accomplishing with infinite ease the mightiest overthrows in their behalf, and restoring them to more than their former prosperity.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:7
segments: Since wicked men are moved by hatred and malice to persecute God's church, he will hold them guilty for all the sufferings which they inflict upon her; while at the same time he uses them as a rod for chastisement and correction.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:8
segments: As the he-goats before the flocks; this is addressed especially to the Jewish rulers and leaders.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:9
segments: All the nations of the earth move in accordance with God's eternal counsels; while they are intent upon the accomplishment of their own selfish schemes, he is bringing to pass, through their instrumentality, his wise and good purposes for the chastisement of Zion, or for her deliverance and enlargement.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:12
segments: Your mother--she that bare you; that is, Babylon, considered as the mother of the people.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:15
segments: She hath given her hand; surrendered herself as vanquished.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:16
segments: They shall turn; the foreigners in Babylon.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:18
segments: As I have punished the king of Assyria; Assyria, with Nineveh its capital, had already fallen in the days of Jeremiah, and was now subject to the Chaldeans.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:20
segments: The outward deliverance of God's people is connected with their inward penitence and return to duty.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:21
segments: Merathaim--Pekod; symbolical names: the first, double rebellion, indicating the character; the second, visitation, the fate of Babylon.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:23
segments:
vv 23-34. 
 
Sometimes God allows wicked nations to accumulate vast power and wealth, so that it seems as if they would be able to trample under foot and break in pieces the whole earth without end.  But he can at any moment open his armory against them, and overwhelm them with the weapons of his indignation.  The examples on record of the sudden fall of mighty monarchies, are a standing manifestation of God's supreme power over all that is called powerful among men.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:26
segments: Cast her up as heaps; heaps of sheaves at the threshing-floor.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:34
segments: To the land; the land of Israel.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:36
segments: Liars; diviners, who deceived the people with lies.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:37
segments: Mingled people; mingled mass of foreigners made up of men of different nations.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:42
segments: They who have oppressed and destroyed their fellow men without mercy, whether natins or individuals, shall be destroyed in like manner.

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:44
segments: Behold--before me; see note

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:45
segments: Shall draw them out; see note

entries.title: Jeremiah 50:46
segments: Haughty and powerful oppressors shall be visited by God with terrible judgments, such as shall fill the inhabitants of the earth with awe and terror.
